arxiv-1803-01121.title: A Spin Analogue of Kerov Polynomials This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on the Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups and Related Topics. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/symmetric-groups-2018.html
arxiv-1803-01121.creator: Sho MATSUMOTO
arxiv-1803-01121.description: Abstract Kerov polynomials describe normalized irreducible characters of the symmetric groups in terms of the free cumulants associated with Young diagrams. We suggest well-suited counterparts of the Kerov polynomials in spin (or projective) representation settings. We show that spin analogues of irreducible characters are polynomials in even free cumulants associated with double diagrams of strict partitions.

arxiv-2201-11631.creator: Monica Vitali
arxiv-2201-11631.description: Abstract Data centers energy demand is increasing. While a great deal of effort has been made to reduce the amount of CO 2 generated by large cloud providers, too little has been done from the application perspective. We claim that application developers can impact the environmental footprint by enhancing the application design with additional features.

arxiv-2206-11272.title: easyFermi : a graphical interface for performing Fermi -LAT data analyses Journal: Astronomy and Computing
arxiv-2206-11272.creator: Raniere de Menezes 1,2
arxiv-2206-11272.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Raniere de Menezes 1,2. Since its launch in 2008, the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) allowed us to peek into the extremely energetic side of the Universe with unprecedented sensitivity and resolution. The tools available for analyzing Fermi -LAT data are the Fermitools and Fermipy , both of which can be scripted in Python and run via command lines in a terminal or in web-based interactive computing platforms.

arxiv-2208-12334.title: Footprint of Publication Selection Bias on Meta-Analyses in Medicine, Environmental Sciences, Psychology, and Economics
arxiv-2208-12334.creator: František Bartoš*, Maximilian Maier*, Eric-Jan Wagenmakers, Franziska Nippold, Hristos Doucouliagos, John P. A. Ioannidis, Willem M. Otte, Martina Sladekova, Teshome K. Deresssa, Stephan B. Bruns, Daniele Fanelli, T.D. Stanley
arxiv-2208-12334.description: Abstract Publication selection bias undermines the systematic accumulation of evidence. To assess the extent of this problem, we survey over 68,000 meta-analyses containing over 700,000 effect size estimates from medicine (67,386/597,699) , environmental sciences (199/12,707) , psychology (605/23,563) , and economics (327/91,421) .

arxiv-2304-06910.title: HCAM - Hierarchical Cross Attention Model for Multi-modal Emotion Recognition
arxiv-2304-06910.creator: Soumya Dutta, Sriram Ganapathy
arxiv-2304-06910.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Soumya Dutta, Sriram Ganapathy. Emotion recognition in conversations is challenging due to the multi-modal nature of the emotion expression. We propose a hierarchical cross-attention model (HCAM) approach to multi-modal emotion recognition using a combination of recurrent and co-attention neural network models. The input to the model consists of two modalities, i) audio data, processed through a learnable wav2vec approach and, ii) text data represented using a bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) model.

arxiv-2305-18901.title: Policy Optimization for Continuous Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2305-18901.creator: Hanyang Zhao Wenpin Tang David D. Yao
arxiv-2305-18901.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hanyang Zhao Wenpin Tang David D. Yao. We study reinforcement learning (RL) in the setting of continuous time and space, for an infinite horizon with a discounted objective and the underlying dynamics driven by a stochastic differential equation. Built upon recent advances in the continuous approach to RL, we develop a notion of occupation time (specifically for a discounted objective), and show how it can be effectively used to derive performance-difference and local-approximation formulas.

arxiv-2408-04292.description: Abstract A heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe 2 \text{UTe}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} has been a strong candidate for a spin-triplet superconductor. Experiments on UTe 2 \text{UTe}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} under pressure have been vigorously conducted, and rich phase diagrams have been suggested. Multiple superconducting phases exist in the pressure region of 0 ≤ P < 1.8 ​ GPa 0\leq P<1.

arxiv-2411-00445.creator: Bob Osano
arxiv-2411-00445.description: Abstract In this study, we deviate from the traditional examination of the evolving universe through the scale factor and instead consider a parameter χ M ​ E \chi_{\scriptscriptstyle ME} , defined by the ratio of two competing energy densities: matter (DM) and dynamic dark energy (DDE).

arxiv-2412-08987.title: Isogeometric Analysis for the Pricing of Financial Derivatives with Nonlinear Models: Convertible Bonds and Options
arxiv-2412-08987.creator: Rakhymzhan Kazbek, Yogi Erlangga, Yerlan Amanbek, Dongming Wei
arxiv-2412-08987.description: Abstract Computational efficiency is essential for enhancing the accuracy and practicality of pricing complex financial derivatives. In this paper, we discuss Isogeometric Analysis (IGA) for valuing financial derivatives, modeled by two nonlinear Black-Scholes PDEs: the Leland model for European call with transaction costs and the AFV model for convertible bonds with default options.

arxiv-2509-18222.title: Mathematical Methods in the Applied Sciences. 2021. Vol.44. No.14. P.11514-11525.
arxiv-2509-18222.creator: Predator-Prey Models with Memory and Kicks:
arxiv-2509-18222.description: Abstract In this paper, we proposed new predator-prey models that take into account memory and kicks. Memory is understood as the dependence of current behavior on the history of past behavior. The equations of these proposed models are generalizations of the Lotka-Volterra and Kolmogorov equations by using the Caputo fractional derivative of non-integer order and periodic kicks.

arxiv-2509-21231.title: SEEC: Stable End-Effector Control with Model-Enhanced Residual Learning for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation * Equal Contribution. Project Co-lead. 1 Tsinghua University, 100084, China 2 Stanford University, CA
arxiv-2509-21231.creator: Jaehwi Jang, Zhuoheng Wang, Ziyi Zhou, Feiyang Wu, Ye Zhao
arxiv-2509-21231.description: Abstract Arm end-effector stabilization is essential for humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, yet it remains challenging due to the high degrees of freedom and inherent dynamic instability of bipedal robot structures. Previous model-based controllers achieve precise end-effector control but rely on precise dynamics modeling and estimation, which often struggle to capture real-world factors (e.g., friction and backlash) and thus degrade in practice.

arxiv-2512-00601.title: Clinical-R1: Empowering Large Language Models for Faithful and Comprehensive Reasoning with Clinical Objective Relative Policy Optimization
arxiv-2512-00601.creator: Boyang Gu, Hongjian Zhou, Bradley Max Segal, Jinge Wu, Zeyu Cao, Hantao Zhong, Lei Clifton, Fenglin Liu, David A. Clifton
arxiv-2512-00601.description: Abstract Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have shown strong reasoning capabilities through large-scale pretraining and post-training reinforcement learning, demonstrated by DeepSeek-R1. However, current post-training methods, such as Grouped Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), mainly reward correctness, which is not aligned with the multi-dimensional objectives required in high-stakes fields such as medicine, where reasoning must also be faithful and comprehensive.

arxiv-2602-12422.title: CacheMind : From Miss Rates to Why — Natural-Language, Trace-Grounded Reasoning for Cache Replacement CCS: Computer systems organization Architectures CCS: Computing methodologies Information extraction CCS: Software and its engineering Software notations and tools CCS: Computing methodologies Causa

arxiv-2602-12422.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Kaushal Mhapsekar, Azam Ghanbari, Bita Aslrousta, Samira Mirbagher-Ajorpaz. Cache replacement remains a challenging problem in CPU microarchitecture, often addressed using hand-crafted heuristics, limiting cache performance. Cache data analysis requires parsing millions of trace entries with manual filtering, making the process slow and non-interactive. To address this, we introduce CacheMind , a conversational tool that uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to enable semantic reasoning over cache traces.

pmc-11444587.title: Bladder transitional cell carcinoma anatomic primary site as a predictor of survival and mortality: a population-based retrospective cohort study
pmc-11444587.creator: Ali Hemade, Souheil Hallit
pmc-11444587.description: Background:Bladder cancer is a heterogeneous disease with varying prognostic outcomes based on the primary tumor site within the bladder. This study aims to evaluate the impact of tumor location on overall survival and cancer-specific survival in bladder cancer patients.Methods:The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database.

pmc-11545950.title: Complex Thoracic Aortic Diseases and Surgery: A Quest for the Golden Fleece
pmc-11545950.creator: Dimitrios E. Magouliotis, Thanos Athanasiou
pmc-11545950.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In recent times, the appropriate management of complex aortic diseases represents the modern Golden Fleece for every aortic surgeon, along with all the adjacent specialties. Starting from the point of understanding the biology and pathogenesis of aortic diseases [2,3] and moving to enhance our diagnostic and treatment armamentarium [4,5], we can proudly admit that we have made tremendous steps forward over the last decades in our quest for the Golden Fleece of the appropriate management of complex aortic diseases.

pmc-12379404.creator: Ayse Yildiz, Ramazan Yildiz, Onur Camli, Musa Eymir
pmc-12379404.description: BackgroundGeneralized joint hypermobility (GJH) is a highly prevalent condition that affects a person’s exercise tolerance and is frequently associated with joint injuries. This study aimed to evaluate body composition and aerobic/ anaerobic power in young adults with asymptomatic GJH.MethodsSixty university students aged 18–25 years (30 with GJH, 30 controls) participated in the study.

pmc-12497391.title: Evaluating Clinical and Radiological Outcomes of Ilizarov Ligamentotaxis and Volar Locked Plating in AO Type C2 and C3 Distal Radius Fractures: A Two-Year Prospective Observational Study

pmc-12497391.description: Background: Soft tissue compromise, articular incongruity, and comminution make treating complex intra-articular distal radius fractures (AO types C2 and C3) very difficult. We hypothesized that volar locked plating (VLP) would provide superior clinical, radiological, and functional outcomes compared to Ilizarov ligamentotaxis in the management of AO type C2/C3 distal radius fractures.

pmc-12628962.title: Sequential intramural pregnancies in the right uterine cornu after the transfer of two embryos in a single cycle: a case report and literature review
pmc-12628962.creator: Litong Yin, Zhaolin Gong, Xinyu Xiao, Xin Li, Xia Yu, Ling Cui, Yonghong Lin, Fang Wang, Li He
pmc-12628962.description: BackgroundIntramural pregnancy (IMP) is a subtype of ectopic pregnancy that can lead to life-threatening uterine rupture and severe hemorrhage. However, the clinical manifestations of IMP are nonspecific, making early clinical recognition challenging. This study reports a case in which two fresh embryos were transferred in the same cycle, and subsequent intramural pregnancies occurred twice.

pmc-13035075.title: Acceptability and Feasibility of Longitudinal Sampling for Sexually Transmitted Enteric Infections in Gay, Bisexual, and Other Men Who Have Sex With Men (GBMSM): Prospective Cohort Pilot Study Conducted in 2022 in South East England

There remain important gaps in our understanding of how STEI transmission is sustained that repeated collection of samples could help to address.

pmc-13262345.title: Fast Generation of Simulation-Quality Structural Ensembles of Mixed-Chirality Cyclic Peptides via Diffusion Models
pmc-13262345.creator: Nomindari Bayaraa, Maxim Secor, Marc L. Descoteaux, Yu-Shan Lin
pmc-13262345.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cyclic peptides are an emerging therapeutic modality, with recent computational efforts focusing on the design of cyclic peptides that predominantly adopt a single conformation. However, many cyclic peptides adopt multiple conformations in solution, existing as structural ensembles. This conformational flexibility is often integral to their function: chameleonic switching between alternative states can enhance membrane permeability, and specific conformations may be required for molecular recognition and binding.

This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the individual and combined effects of key SES indicators, including marital status, household income, and residence, on diagnosis, treatment, and survival outcomes, and to develop a composite SES risk score in patients with primary bone cancer.MethodsPrimary bone cancer patients diagnosed between 2000 and 2022 were identified

pmc-13434656.title: Enhancing sleep slow waves with auditory stimulation in people with Parkinson’s disease: a randomized proof-of-concept trial
pmc-13434656.creator: Simon J Schreiner, Jana Horlacher, Sara Fattinger, Bettina Markert, Klavs Renerts, Luzius Brogli, Lydia Kämpf, Maurizio Scandella, Rositsa Poryazova, Philipp O Valko, Laura Ferster, Renske Sassenburg, Valeria Jaramillo, Giulia Da Poian, Caroline Lustenberger, Walter Karlen, Reto Huber, Christian R B
pmc-13434656.description: Background: Deep sleep supports restorative functions and has emerged as a potential therapeutic target in neurodegenerative diseases, such as Parkinson’s (PD). Phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) non-invasively enhances slow waves, the electrophysiological hallmark of deep sleep. Objectives: To investigate, for the first time, whether PTAS can be successfully applied in PD, using a wearable device at home.

pmc-13473330.title: Competition and equity in NHS specialty training, 2021–2024: longitudinal cohort analysis of protected-characteristic outcomes
pmc-13473330.creator: Dinesh Aggarwal, Meera Roy-Chowdhury, Nicola Xiang, Sharon J Peacock
pmc-13473330.description: Objectives:To evaluate recruitment equity for NHS specialty training posts between 2021–2024, characterising demographics, quantifying appointment disparities by protected characteristics and assessing temporal trends.Design:Longitudinal cohort study using national recruitment data via annual Freedom of Information requests.Setting:National Health Service, UK.Participants:All medical and surgical specialty training applications to NHS England (2021–2024).Main outcome measures:Application success by protected characteristics.Results:Of 214,893 applications, 52,998 (24.7%) were appointed.

pmc-13506737.title: Yoga-based meditation improves self-regulation and well-being in medical students: a pilot study
pmc-13506737.creator: Felipe Rojas-Thomas, Ignacia Cantwell, Claudio Artigas, Diego Garrido, Jessica Goset, María Jose Olivares, Joaquín Araya, Benjamin Ibañez, Antonella Pereira, María Carolina Otero, Luis Sebastián Contreras-Huerta, Ricardo Ramirez-Barrantes
pmc-13506737.description: IntroductionSelf-regulation enables students to effectively apply their metacognitive abilities to reach academic objectives and enhance their well-being, which is essential in academic high-pressure situations such as medical education. However, many medical students have difficulty managing their cognitive and emotional responses to continued academic pressure and the clinical demands placed upon them.

pmc-13510514.title: Eisenia andrei and Tenebrio molitor Divergently Restructure the Bacteriome and Mycobiome of Sewage Sludge with Contrasting Biosafety Consequences

pmc-13510514.description: The use of invertebrates for sewage sludge bioconversion offers a sustainable strategy for waste valorization, yet species-specific effects on microbial communities and biosafety remain unclear. Here, we compared the impacts of the earthworm Eisenia andrei (Ea) and the mealworm Tenebrio molitor (Tm) on the bacteriomes and mycobiomes of sewage sludge (ss) using 16S rRNA and ITS amplicon sequencing.
